This centers the Gaussian projection guard band on the view rather than the optical axis to prevent distortion of Gaussians elongated along the view direction [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the Gaussian projection guard band is centered on the view rather than the optical axis to prevent distortion of Gaussians elongated along the view direction. The provided evidence (Source [S1] notes and passages) explicitly confirms this: 'The projected Gaussian centres used for the covariance Jacobian were clamped to a guard band around the optical axis... With an off-centre projection... visible Gaussians lie away from the axis and were clamped too, which distorted the footprints of Gaussians elongated along the view direction. The band is now centred on the view.' This matches the claim exactly.
supported

The source text explicitly confirms: 'The colour image is unchanged' and 'GsplatConfig::outputDepth makes a backend also write a per-pixel depth buffer (NDC depth...)'. Therefore, every fact in the claim is supported by the evidence.

The implementation also fixed a bug related to off-centre projection guard bands [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in the commit message 'fix: centre the Gaussian projection guard band on off-centre views' and describes how projected Gaussian centres were previously clamped to a guard band around the optical axis, causing distortion with off-centre projections. The fix involved centering the guard band on the view instead. This directly supports the claim that the implementation fixed a bug related to off-centre projection guard bands.

This method extends Gaussian Splatting rasterization to produce a per-pixel depth buffer (NDC depth, $+\infty$ where no surface is visible) while respecting the variable opacity of the Gaussians [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the method extends Gaussian Splatting backends to write a per-pixel depth buffer (NDC depth, +inf where no surface) via the `outputDepth` configuration flag. It details how this is achieved while respecting opacity (using median depth for transmittance crossing in the compute backend and nearest depth with opacity >= 0.5 in the raster backend). All specific claims in the statement are present in the provided notes and passages.
